title: On‑Prem Kubernetes: Proactive Upgrade Playbook + Terraform module notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for planning and executing proactive, low-downtime upgrades of on‑prem Kubernetes clusters (bare metal & vSphere). It also captures notes for Terraform modules used in provisioning control/worker planes and BMC/vSphere resources. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: checklists, commands, failure modes, and module-level guidance for the infra repo.

Scope and goals:
- Supported environments: bare-metal with IPMI/BMC provisioning and vSphere VMs managed by Terraform.
- Goals: 
  - Zero-to-minimal customer-facing downtime for control plane and worker upgrades.
  - Reproducible Terraform workflow for bootstrapping/repairing clusters.
  - Clear rollback and node-replacement playbooks.
- Not in scope: application-level migration strategies (assume apps have PodDisruptionBudgets or can tolerate rolling restarts).

Assumptions and preconditions:
- Cluster created with kubeadm (or upstream kubeadm-like flow) and containerd as CRI.
- All nodes are reachable by the control plane and have working NTP (chrony) and DNS entries.
- External load balancer in front of control plane (HAProxy or NSX) with health checks.
- Persistent storage: Rook (Ceph) or external NFS; operations differ — see Storage section.
- Terraform state is locked (remote backend like S3-compatible or HashiCorp Cloud).

Inventory checklist before upgrade:
- kubectl cluster-info and node list 
  - `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
- Control plane node health: `kubectl get componentstatuses` and `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide`
- API server latency check: sample `curl` to LB VIP and to each control-plane ip:443
- Backup: etcd snapshot + upload to object storage
  - `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=... --cert=... --key=...`
- Kubeconfig export: store a copy off-cluster
- Prometheus/alerts: ensure no unresolved critical alerts (or acknowledge them before starting)

Pre-upgrade quick wins (reduce blast radius):
- Ensure PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs) exist for critical apps
- Ensure fewest number of daemonsets that will be restarted (eg node-exporter fine)
- Confirm nodeAutoUpgrade not enabled in Terraform (we want manual control)

Terraform module notes (infra repo):
- Module topology: split modules for (1) provisioning primitives (bmc/ipmi or vsphere), (2) base OS image + cloud-init, (3) network/dns, (4) k8s-cluster (kubeadm configs, bootstrap tokens, kubeconfigs), (5) load-balancer and monitoring hooks.
- Recommended variable patterns: minimal required in root module, everything else defaulted in child modules. Keep secrets out of repo: use vault/TF_VARs or KMS-encrypted file.
- Important module variables: `bmc_username`, `bmc_password_secret_id`, `image_url`, `ssh_pub_keys`, `cluster_name`, `kubeadm_config_map`, `control_plane_count`, `worker_count`, `vsphere_datacenter`, `vsphere_datastore`, `lb_vip`.
- Outputs to expose: `kubeconfig`, `control_plane_ips`, `lb_vip`, `bmc_inventory_ids`, `terraform_provider_versions` (for audits).
- Apply order: 1) provisioning (BMC/vSphere) 2) base OS + cloud-init 3) network/dns 4) LB 5) bootstrap control plane 6) join workers. Use `-target` sparingly for repair.
- Tainted resource policy: prefer recreating worker VMs via `terraform taint module.worker.vm[...]` over in-place upgrades for kernel/OS drift. Record tainted indexes in PR description.
- Recommended provider pinning: `hashicorp/vsphere ~> 2.4` and `projektfarm/ipmi ~> 0.3` (adjust to current repo).

Provisioning & bootstrapping notes (bare-metal):
- PXE/iPXE steps: keep a versioned iPXE script in infra repo. Example snippet to inject the image URL and cloud-init metadata: `kernel http://images.internal/vmlinuz initrd=initramfs.img ip=dhcp url=$IMAGE_URL console=ttyS1`
- Cloud-init: include `runcmd` steps to register SSH key, write kubeadm join token placeholder, and call `systemd` unit to wait for the provisioning service.
- BMC: ensure BMC users have limited privileges; use out-of-band network. For IPMI flashing and power cycle tests run a dry-run before maintenance window.

Control plane upgrade strategy (kubeadm flow):
1) Backup etcd snapshot + verify integrity.
2) Upgrade kubeadm binary on first control plane node.
3) Run `kubeadm upgrade plan` to list supported versions.
4) Upgrade control plane one node at a time: 
   - `kubectl cordon <node>`
   - `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='!critical'` (adjust pod-selector for infra pods)
   - `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y` on that node (control-plane upgrade path per kubeadm docs)
   - Restart kubelet if needed and verify `kubectl get cs` and `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide`
   - Uncordon once healthy: `kubectl uncordon <node>`
5) Repeat for remaining control-plane nodes.
6) Upgrade kubelets and kubectl on workers (rolling, drain each worker, upgrade kubelet, restart, uncordon).

Notes for low-downtime control-plane upgrades:
- Keep the LB in front of control plane with health checks that tolerate short API restarts.
- Do not upgrade two control plane nodes at the same time unless you have quorum considerations and etcd cluster resilience tested.
- Validate webhook admission controllers and CRD conversion webhooks; if they block, pause their pods before control-plane upgrades.

Worker upgrade strategy (rolling):
- For each worker: 
  1) `kubectl cordon <worker>`
  2) `kubectl drain <worker> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 
  3) Recreate or upgrade OS/kernel/container runtime (use orchestration: SSH+Ansible or terraform replace)
  4) Upgrade kubelet & kube-proxy binary to target version 
  5) `systemctl restart kubelet` and verify `kubectl get nodes` shows Ready
  6) `kubectl uncordon <worker>`
- If large stateful workloads present, ensure successful failover of PVs (Rook) or increase PDBs accordingly.

Stateful storage (Rook/Ceph) specific guidance:
- Never drain more than one Ceph OSD per node at a time. Prefer OSD graceful eviction using `ceph osd crush reweight` and `ceph osd out` if replacing nodes.
- Upgrade Rook operator first, verify health, then upgrade Ceph cluster. Follow upstream Rook docs for the operator lifecycle.
- For external NFS, ensure the server can handle reconnects; plan a maintenance window if you need to move NFS pods.

Rollback and recovery patterns:
- Etcd rollback: restore snapshot to a restored cluster or a single-control-plane node (documented step-by-step with etcdctl restore flags).
- Node failure mid-upgrade: if a control-plane node fails during upgrade, remove it from LB, complete the upgrade on remaining nodes, then reprovision the failed node from terraform (taint + apply) and rejoin.
- Recreate worker: `terraform taint module.workers.vm[index]` -> `terraform apply` will recreate and join via cloud-init join token or SSM hook.
- If control plane becomes unhealthy and quorum is lost, follow emergency steps: 
  - Isolate offending control plane nodes, attempt to restore etcd from last known good snapshot to one node, then scale control plane up.

Pre-flight checklist (run immediately before window):
- All backups taken & verified (etcd snapshot, config backups)
- Slack channel + paging on-call + runbook owner present
- Block automated CI/CD deploys to cluster during upgrade
- Firewall and NAT rules checked so LB health checks will succeed
- A copy of terraform state and working directory available on jump host

Quick commands and cheatsheet:
- List versions: `kubectl version --short`
- Run etcd snapshot (on control plane): see earlier etcdctl example
- Kubeadm upgrade plan: `kubeadm upgrade plan`
- Drain worker: `kubectl drain node-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- Recreate VM (terraform): `terraform taint module.workers.vm[3] && terraform apply -target=module.workers.module.vm[3]`

vSphere-specific notes:
- Use the vsphere module to create templates; keep templates immutable and version-tagged.
- Use vCenter alarms to detect VM-level issues during the window.
- Prefer vSphere Tools upgrades outside the kernel/CRI upgrade window.
- If performing storage vMotion or datastore maintenance, ensure CSI driver is updated first and PVs have `WaitForFirstConsumer` or proper topology.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- API server flapping: temporarily increase LB health-check threshold and give control plane more time to become healthy; pause upgrade and investigate controller-manager logs.
- Node stuck in NotReady after upgrade: check CRI socket, containerd logs, and certificate expiry. If kubelet fails for kernel reasons, revert to known-good kernel or reprovision VM.
- Etcd quorum loss: restore snapshot to new control plane; follow emergency restore playbook.

Post-upgrade validation checklist:
- All nodes Ready and schedulable
- Critical system pods in kube-system are Running and Ready
- Smoke tests for key APIs (list namespaces, create job, create CRD, delete)
- Load testing for control plane if possible (small synthetic load)
- Metrics and dashboards show stable latency and no large increases in API error rates
- Create a short postmortem if anything non-trivial happened

Open TODOs & follow-ups (repo tasks):
- [ ] Add automated preflight check script to infra repo that validates NTP, DNS, LB health, and etcd snapshot.
- [ ] Move BMC secrets into Vault with Kubernetes auth and rotate weekly.
- [ ] Add terraform `plan` -> `apply` gating with a Jenkins/GitHub Actions job that annotates PRs with target nodes.
- [ ] Build a small `drain-and-upgrade` operator that can perform safe rolling upgrades for non-critical apps (RFC in CONFLUENCE-8492).

Notes to the reader: this is a working draft. If you are executing an upgrade, copy this doc into a temporary maintenance doc and stamp your commands into a runbook. If any step is unclear, call the on‑call infra engineer in Slack channel #infra-ops immediately.
